Compute the default checks of a claim

Source: R/csdg_check.R
csdg_check.Rd

Fourth step of the analysis-first interface: computes the properties that a claim derived with claim_relies_mainly(), claim_top_k(), claim_order(), or claim_direction() requires, with the default criteria described in the article, and records each as a csdg_evidence_record(). csdg_assess() then applies the decision rule with csdg_adjudicate_claim().

The checks are:

  • G0a (specification): the claim and its six scope elements, generated from the analysis (supported).

  • G0b (measurement and data): open until the researcher judges it with csdg_judge(), for example csdg_check(claim, imp, judgments = csdg_judge("G0b", supported(), note = "...")). Whether the variables were measured, coded, and sampled so that they cover what the claim names cannot be computed from the data, so an assessment stays unresolved until G0b is judged. A claim that names constructs (refers_to = "constructs") also needs validity evidence for them.

  • G1 (predictive performance, context): held-out loss of each covered learner versus the model without predictors.

  • G2 (content): the claim's words translated into margins on the learner average. For claim_relies_mainly() and claim_top_k(), each named predictor is compared with every predictor that the claim does not name, with the margin "PFI of the named predictor minus factor times the PFI of the other predictor" (factor = 1 for claim_top_k()) and with its own Monte Carlo threshold and corrected interval. The content is supported only if every comparison is supported, contradicted if any is contradicted, and open otherwise, because a predictor with a smaller mean PFI than the largest other predictor can vary more across folds. The observation reports the ratios and margins against the other predictor with the largest mean PFI and the weakest comparison: a contradicted one before an open one before a supported one, and among these the one with the smallest lower bound of its corrected interval. A claim that covers several learners records its content under G6a instead, one row per learner.

  • G2 (minimum importance): each named predictor has a mean PFI of at least min_importance times the learner's improvement over the model without predictors, in the same loss (under G6a for several learners). The observation compares the mean PFI with the minimum in loss units.

  • G2 (procedure): the claim names marginal PFI; if grouped or conditional PFI was computed (csdg_importance() with groups, conditional, or strata), a reversal of the claim's content contradicts this property unless the claim was worded with marginal_only = TRUE ("Under marginal permutation"). A comparison counts only if the marginal result holds for that learner; otherwise the perturbation changes nothing. For a ranking claim, as for the content, each named predictor is compared with every group of grouped PFI that contains no named predictor and, with conditional PFI, with every other predictor if either of the two is conditioned; the observation shows the weakest comparison of each named predictor.

  • G2 (dependence): for each named predictor, the \(R^2\) of a linear regression of that predictor on all other predictors (factors one-hot encoded; for a factor predictor, the largest \(R^2\) over its level indicators), computed on the data of the importance (the rows of the task, complete cases). A named predictor is flagged if its \(R^2\) is at least max_r2 or if it belongs to a group in dependent_groups, unless conditional or grouped PFI covers it; marginal PFI may then be redistributed between dependent predictors. Conditional PFI of the predictor covers it. Grouped PFI covers it only if its group also contains the predictors on which it depends: the \(R^2\) of the predictor on the predictors outside the group must stay below max_r2, and the group must contain the other members of its groups in dependent_groups. A group that leaves out such predictors permutes the predictor without them, so marginal PFI can still be redistributed to them, as with a block of indices that omits offsetting indices. A flag is an unresolved threat that leaves G2 open, or context with marginal_only = TRUE; without a flag, the \(R^2\) values are reported as context. Unlike a pairwise correlation, the \(R^2\) also detects a predictor that other predictors determine jointly.

  • G5 (stability): in each fold, the claim's selection rule is applied again (for example, the top k and the ratio are recomputed; ties at the cutoff do not count as reproduced), and the share of folds that reproduce the result must be at least stability; neighboring cutoffs are reported. For a direction claim, the change between the percentiles and, for a claim that the predictions rise or fall, the adjacent grid points of the ALE are checked in each fold (see below). A failing fold counts only if it fails beyond Monte Carlo error (with a two-sided Holm adjustment when every fold is required) and by at least the smallest relevant difference; otherwise it is undecided. The property is supported if enough folds hold, contradicted if too few would hold even if every undecided fold held, and open otherwise.

  • G6a (models): when the claim covers several learners, its content and minimum importance are required for each; otherwise the other learners' results are reported as context.

Status of a margin (content, and the grouped or conditional comparisons of the procedure): the margin is supported if it holds beyond Monte Carlo error and, with interval_rule = "open_if_inconclusive", the lower bound of its corrected resampled t interval (csdg_learner_pfi_interval()) is at least the smallest relevant difference; it is contradicted if it fails beyond Monte Carlo error and the upper bound is at most minus the smallest relevant difference; otherwise it is open. The rule is symmetric: the article treats a property that hinges on a difference whose corrected interval includes zero, or excludes it by less than the smallest relevant difference, as open, in either direction. With interval_rule = "report_only", the interval is only reported. The minimum importance is supported if the mean PFI is at least the minimum beyond Monte Carlo error, open within Monte Carlo error, and contradicted if it is below beyond Monte Carlo error and (by default) the upper bound of its corrected interval is below the minimum. For direction claims, the change must reach min_change with its lower bound, and a contradiction needs a change in the opposite direction whose upper bound is at most -min_change. A fold reproduces a claim that the predictions rise with a predictor (claim_direction() with monotone = TRUE, the default) only if the change between the percentiles is at least min_change and no decrease of the ALE between adjacent grid points in the range between the percentiles exceeds min_change, as the article's default criterion for "rise" requires (for "fall", no increase exceeds it); the stability property counts the folds in which both hold, and its observation reports the largest such decrease (or increase). A claim that the predictions are higher (or lower) at the upper than at the lower percentile (monotone = FALSE) needs only the change in each fold.

The Monte Carlo rule compares a difference with the .975 quantile (for level = 0.95) of the t distribution with R - 1 degrees of freedom times its Monte Carlo standard error (csdg_pfi_mc_difference()); a decisive difference within Monte Carlo error leaves the property open. When every fold is required, failing folds are compared in a two-sided Holm step-down, as in the article: ordered by the ratio of the difference to its Monte Carlo standard error, the i-th failing fold is compared with qt(1 - (1 - level) / (2 * (K - i + 1)), R - 1) times its standard error (with level = 0.95, qt(1 - 0.025 / K, R - 1) for the largest reversal), and from the first fold within its threshold on, the remaining failing folds count as within Monte Carlo error.

A claim derived from a csdg_loco() result is checked in the same way on LOCO: the content, the minimum importance, and the stability use the LOCO fold values, and the Monte Carlo rule does not apply, because LOCO is computed once per fold. Its wording names refits without single predictors, so grouped LOCO is reported with the procedure but does not contradict it, and the dependence screen is context.

Sources of the default criteria: 1% of the improvement (minimum importance), 9 of 10 folds (stability), and a factor of 2 for "relies mainly on" are conventions of the article; the corrected interval rule is its recommendation; min_change and max_r2 are package defaults. Each record states the source of its criterion.

Usage

csdg_check(
  claim,
  x,
  min_importance = 0.01,
  stability = 0.9,
  min_difference = NULL,
  min_change = NULL,
  max_r2 = 0.5,
  dependent_groups = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  interval_rule = c("open_if_inconclusive", "report_only"),
  judgments = NULL,
  note = NULL,
  max_cor = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'CSDGCheck'
format(x, width = getOption("width", 80L), details = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'CSDGCheck'
print(x, width = getOption("width", 80L), details = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'CSDGCheck'
as.data.table(x, keep.rownames = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'CSDGCheck'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'CSDGCheck'
plot(x, ...)

Arguments

claim

A claim from claim_relies_mainly(), claim_top_k(), claim_order(), or claim_direction().

x

For csdg_check(): a csdg_importance() result on the same data, with the same loss and the learners the claim covers, or a csdg_loco() result for a claim derived from LOCO. It may differ from the result the claim was derived from, for example by added conditional PFI. For direction claims, a csdg_effect() or csdg_fit() result also works. Use csdg_confirm() for new data. For the methods: a CSDGCheck object.

min_importance

Minimum importance as a share of each covered learner's mean improvement over the model without predictors (default 1%).

stability

Required share of folds; the criterion is "in at least ceiling(stability * K) of the K folds".

min_difference

Smallest relevant difference in loss units; defaults to min_importance times each learner's improvement.

min_change

For direction claims: smallest relevant change of the prediction between the two percentiles, which for a claim that the predictions rise (or fall) also bounds the decrease (or increase) between adjacent grid points; defaults to 0.02 on the probability scale (classification) or 0.1 times the standard deviation of the outcome (regression).

max_r2

\(R^2\) of a named predictor on all other predictors from which it is flagged by the dependence screen (default 0.5, a package default; for two predictors, it corresponds to an absolute correlation of about .71).

dependent_groups

Optional named list of character vectors: groups of predictors that the researcher knows to be dependent (for example items of one scale or recodings of one variable). A named predictor in such a group is flagged whatever its \(R^2\), unless conditional PFI covers it or grouped PFI of a group that contains the whole declared group covers it.

level

Confidence level of the corrected interval and of the Monte Carlo quantile.

interval_rule

"open_if_inconclusive" (default; see Description) or "report_only".

judgments

Optional csdg_judge() result or list of them, for properties that cannot be computed, such as G0b.

note

Optional note stored with the check.

max_cor

Deprecated since version 0.3.0; replaced by max_r2. If given, max_r2 = max_cor^2 is used with a deprecation warning, which flags at least the predictors that the pairwise screen of earlier versions flagged.

width

For print(): line width.

details

For print(): if TRUE, also prints the criterion and the relevance of each row.

...

Ignored.

keep.rownames

Ignored.

object

A CSDGCheck object.

Value

A CSDGCheck list with claim, criteria (fixed values, their sources, and the date they were fixed), table (one row per property or context entry: gate, gate_name, check, learner, role, property, criterion, observation, relevance, status, and summary), details (the computed numbers per check; per learner, details$content holds every comparison of a named with another predictor in comparisons, the weakest comparison of each named predictor in margins, and the other predictor with the largest mean PFI in largest_other; details$dependence holds the dependence screen, with the \(R^2\) of each named predictor on all other predictors, the group of grouped PFI that contains it with its \(R^2\) on the predictors outside the group (r2_outside), covered, and flagged), records (one csdg_evidence_record() per row), plan (csdg_gate_plan()), measurement, explanation, judgments, note, origin, and source. print() shows gate, check, status, and observation (details = TRUE adds criterion and relevance), plot() draws the fold values against the criterion, and as.data.table() returns table. Each call is added to the claim log (csdg_claim_log()).

See also

csdg_assess(), csdg_judge(), csdg_confirm()

Examples

set.seed(1)
n = 200
x = data.frame(a = rnorm(n), b = rnorm(n), c = rnorm(n))
x$y = 2 * x$a + x$b + rnorm(n)
task = mlr3::as_task_regr(x, target = "y", id = "toy")
fits = csdg_fit(task, list(tree = mlr3::lrn("regr.rpart")), folds = 3, seed = 1)
imp = csdg_importance(fits, repetitions = 5, seed = 2)
claim = claim_relies_mainly(imp, k = 1)
# G0b stays open until the researcher judges the measurement and the data
csdg_assess(csdg_check(claim, imp))
#> <CSDG assessment> Decision tree relies mainly on a.
#>   Unresolved (exploratory)
#>   Specification (G0a) supported | Measurement and data (G0b) open | Content
#>   (G2) supported | Minimum importance (G2) supported | Procedure (G2) supported
#>   | Stability (G5) supported
#>   Measurement and data (G0b) is open: measurement and data not yet judged; use
#>   csdg_judge("G0b", ...). The computed properties are supported; pass a
#>   judgment of G0b with `judgments =` to complete the assessment.
#>   Decision options: revise or withhold
g0b = csdg_judge("G0b", supported(), note = "Simulated variables, measured without error.")
chk = csdg_check(claim, imp, judgments = g0b)
chk
#> <CSDG check> Decision tree relies mainly on a.
#> Criteria (defaults, see ?csdg_check): minimum importance 1% of the improvement;
#> at least 3 of 3 folds; Monte Carlo rule; corrected 95% interval must clear the
#> smallest relevant difference.
#> gate  check               status        observation
#> G0a   specification       supported     Generated from the analysis: quantity,
#>                                         model, procedure, data, meaning (model
#>                                         description), and use.
#> G0b   measurement         supported     Judged by the researcher: Simulated
#>                                         variables, measured without error.
#> G1    performance         context       Held-out RMSE 1.55 versus 2.42 for the
#>                                         model without predictors (improvement
#>                                         0.874, a reduction by 36%); 3 of 3
#>                                         folds improve.
#> G2    dependence          context       R^2 on the other 2 predictors: a .01;
#>                                         no named predictor reaches .50.
#> G2    content             supported     a 1.48 versus 0.417 for b, the largest
#>                                         other predictor (3.55 times); margin
#>                                         (PFI minus 2 x PFI of b) 0.647 [0.0767,
#>                                         1.22]; weakest of the 2 comparisons
#>                                         with other predictors: a minus 2 x b,
#>                                         0.647 [0.0767, 1.22].
#> G2    minimum importance  supported     a 1.48 versus the minimum importance
#>                                         0.0087 (1% of the improvement of 0.874,
#>                                         from 2.42 to 1.55).
#> G2    procedure           supported     Held-out marginal PFI with RMSE, 5
#>                                         permutations per fold in 3 folds, as
#>                                         the scope names. No grouped or
#>                                         conditional comparison was requested.
#> G5    stability           supported     Selected anew in each fold: 3 of 3
#>                                         folds reproduce the result (cutoff 2: 3
#>                                         of 3).
csdg_assess(chk)
#> <CSDG assessment> Decision tree relies mainly on a.
#>   Met (exploratory)
#>   Specification (G0a) supported | Measurement and data (G0b) supported |
#>   Content (G2) supported | Minimum importance (G2) supported | Procedure (G2)
#>   supported | Stability (G5) supported
#>   On average, a has 3.55 times the PFI of the largest other predictor, b; the
#>   result recurs in 3 of 3 folds. The claim was formulated after the explanation
#>   was inspected; it is established only after a test on new data
#>   (csdg_confirm()).
#>   Decision options: retain
